newsitem.title: NORWAY: Unitor, Norsk Hydro, Kvaerner drag down Oslo bourse.
newsitem.headline: Unitor, Norsk Hydro, Kvaerner drag down Oslo bourse.

text.p: The Oslo bourse ended in negative territory on Friday dragged down by a hand full of stocks after hitting a new all-time high soon after the open.
The Total share index hit 889.46 points in early trade before sliding back to 883.03 points, a loss of 0.11 percent. Turnover was a hefty 1.27 billion crowns.
Brokers attributed the dip to a 21 percent plunge in maritime equipment and services group Unitor and to losses in blue chips Norsk Hydro and Kvaerner.
Unitor tumbled after issuing a profit warning for the third and fourth quarters due to general weak market conditions.
"It's down 20 ticks and I think it should fall another 20. We see no upside in this market," said one broker.
The sell out of Norsk Hydro continued ahead of third quarter results due on Monday with the stock closing 2.50 crowns off at 306 crowns.
Kvaerner fell sharply after shipping group Storli announced its had cancelled an order for two chemical carriers from Kvaerner's Floroe yard.
Kvaerner As fell 15 crowns, or 6.12 percent, to 230 crowns while the Bs finished 10.50 crowns down at 215 crowns.
